In this lesson you will learn about the Hartley Oscillator.
INTRODUCTIONM
Hartley oscillators change the DC operating voltage to a sine wave AC output.
The operation of a Hartley oscillator is the same as a LC oscillator...
Only the number of components in the feedback circuit are different.
Let's begin the lesson on HARTLEY OSCILLATOR OPERATION....................

DISCUSSION
This is a typical Hartley oscillator. Its purpose is to change the DC operating voltage to a sine wave AC output...
It is identified as an LC oscillator by the components in the feedback circuit.
It is identified as a Hartley oscillator by the two inductors.
To analyze circuit operation, divide the oscillator into its two circuits.
The amplifier circuit consists of Q1 and its associated components.
A common emitter amplifier is used. Notice that the transistor is an NPN.
R1 and R2 develop fixed bias on the base of Q1. R3 is the collector load resistor.
Q1 output is routed through the feedback circuit to its input.
This produces oscillations at one particular frequency.
The feedback circuit consists of C1, L1 and L2.............
These components determine the frequency of oscillations.
When the LC tank is resonant, circulating current flows through L1 and L2 in series.
Two inductors are used to reduce the amount of feedback to the amplifier's input.
This prevents over driving the amplifier.
L1 and L2 form an AC voltage divider. The input to the feedback circuit is developed across C1 and L2.
The output to Q1 is developed across C1 and L1.
The required phase shift is accomplished by the feedback circuit.
Checking for normal operation requires calculating the frequency of the resonant circuit.
Then measure the output frequency with an oscilloscope or frequency counter.

This is also a Hartley oscillator. It uses two inductors in the feedback circuit.
The operation is the same. Only the amplifier's biasing and the point where the output is taken from is different.
Fewer components are used and there is no temperature stabilization.
Taking the output of the feedback circuit allows the amplifier to be biased class B or C.plifier to be biased class B or C.
Taking the output from the collector of an amplifier biased class B or C produces a distorted output waveform.
This circuit is also a Hartley oscillator. It uses two inductors.
However, the input to the feedback circuit is from the emitter to the center of L1 and L2.
In this oscillator, the input and output of the feedback circuit must be in phase since the base and emitter signals are in phase.
The in phase condition is accomplished by L1 being in series to the input and output of the amplifier.
The phase of a signal is the same through a series circuit.
The resonant frequency is still calculated the same.
Remember, a Hartley oscillator uses two inductors in the feedback circuit.
This completes the information on HARTLEY OSCILLATOR.......
1. Hartley oscillators are LC oscillators that use two inductors in the feedback circuit.
2. The output of the amplifier is used as its input to produce oscillations.
3. The value of the components in the feedback circuit determine the frequency.
4. Hartley oscillators can be made different. However, they operate the same.
